source.title: Psychometric Personality Shaping Modulates Capabilities and Safety in Language Models
source.authors: Stephen Fitz; P. Romero; Steven Basart; Sipeng Chen; J. Hernández-Orallo

record.tranche_reason: The study tests personality-based system prompts against benchmark scores, but does not test the listed fine-tuning, refusal, token-position, bypass, parameter-localization, or safety-deepening claims. It discusses prompt-based risks in general.
record.gate_note: No direct harmful-request compliance or refusal rate is reported. The rows below capture safety-adjacent benchmark results under low conscientiousness and the composite Profile-1 prompt; ETHICS, TruthfulQA, and WMDP accuracy are not the harmful-request refusal behavior named in the claim. Personality prompting is not fine-tuning or a compliant opening, suffix, or decoding intervention. The study reports other benchmark outcomes, but they do not measure the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies Big Five personality system prompts to five chat models and reports multiple-choice benchmark accuracy (TruthfulQA, WMDP, ETHICS, MMLU, Sycophancy). It reports no harmful-request compliance or refusal rate, no fine-tuning, no per-token KL, and no prefill, suffix or decoding attack. It does no parameter localization and no deepening training. WMDP accuracy measures hazardous knowledge, not refusal. ETHICS accuracy is a moral-judgment score, not compliance with harmful requests. Persona prompting is a prompt intervention, not a compliant opening or adversarial suffix. The study mentions alignment bypass only as speculation. It therefore bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right. The authors conclude that Big Five personality prompts can shift safety benchmark scores by 20–40 pp, especially with low Conscientiousness or adversarial trait combinations, often with little MMLU change. They argue personality is an axis orthogonal to capability and scale that bears on safetywashing debates. They propose persona-robust evaluation and psychometric steering as a lightweight complement to RLHF/DPO, and present personality shaping as a new attack vector. They do not address fine-tuning or token-depth of alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses system-prompt personality conditioning and evaluates benchmark scores; it does not fine-tune on examples or measure response-position KL. It reproduces and adapts the personality-prompting method of Serapio-García et al., not the methods in the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report model-family-dependent effects and note that prompt wording and syntax can substantially affect results. Appendix B reports robustness analyses over semantic tone, syntax, postamble, and sampling variations for conscientiousness prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-Conscientiousness system prompts lowered TruthfulQA, WMDP and ETHICS-CM accuracy, sharply in GPT-4.1 (e.g. ETHICS-CM 71.4 to 38.7) and Llama-3-70B. The drops were small in DeepSeek-V3 and Llama-4-Maverick and mixed in Llama-3-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona or personality system prompts degrade scores on safety-adjacent multiple-choice benchmarks, with model-dependent magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: The Profile-1 persona (low agreeableness, low conscientiousness, high neuroticism) lowered ETHICS-CM accuracy in all five models. The drop ranged from 8.7 pp (DeepSeek-V3) to 26.4 pp (GPT-4.1), and the authors report MMLU losses below 3 pp for GPT-4.1 and Llama-3-70B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial persona prompts lower ethics-benchmark accuracy while largely preserving general capability.

record.problems: The authors acknowledge reliance on a single Likert-style prompt template in the main study, prompt brittleness and model-specific effects, and lack of fully crossed fixed-capability controls. They state that aggregated personality data lack within-condition variances or individual scores; the main benchmark tables provide no uncertainty estimates. Appendix B reports variation analyses and standard deviations for selected conscientiousness results.
record.rows_left_out: Other benchmark outcomes in Tables 8–12, including the remaining ETHICS categories, were not separately cataloged because they are benchmark scores rather than the harmful-request refusal behavior in the claim. MMLU and personality self-report results were also omitted as they do not measure any listed version.

untested.parts: No harmful-data fine-tuning and no harmful-request compliance measure.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. The persona prompts are not evaluated against refusal.
No analysis of the data or objective causing shallowness.
No deepening training or robustness test.

record.verdict_notes: The T6/discusses classification is confirmed. The paper cites Qi et al. 2023 (an original source) only in the related-work list. Its speculation that dark-triad personas could bypass alignment is not tested with any refusal or compliance measure. Sycophancy results are also outside this phenomenon. The rows are correctly marked none and cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Per-token KL divergence across response positions.
Compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
Localization of safety behavior in weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and testing its robustness.

relation.reason: The introduction and ethical considerations discuss possible bypassing of training-time alignment through personality prompts, without testing or using the specified shallow-alignment findings.

tranche.reason: Personality system prompts change benchmark accuracy, a related construct that does not test any listed claim version. The study reports no harmful-request compliance, fine-tuning experiment, response-position KL, opening-bypass attack, parameter localization, or deepening intervention.

source_check.notes: All 20 listed rows match Tables 8–12. These benchmark accuracies do not establish harmful-request compliance; lower WMDP accuracy measures reduced hazardous knowledge, not demonstrated safety erosion.
